verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents a Private Cloud offering: a dedicated, isolated managed instance on AWS or Azure, with region choice for data-residency requirements. That covers the 'private instance' and data-location parts of the story. The only evidence touching 'my own database' is a custom database connection used to migrate users into Auth0, and nothing shows a self-managed or self-hosted deployment, so control stays within Auth0-managed infrastructure. Missing for 10: self-managed/self-hosted deployment, documented ability to keep user data permanently in the customer's own database (beyond migration), independent corroboration of Private Cloud isolation.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can control where the auth system and its user data run — self-managed deployment, private instance, or my own database

citations.quote: Compare Auth0 Private Cloud-managed service deployment options on AWS and Azure to choose a dedicated, isolated environment that meets your data-residency, performance, and guaranteed RPS requirements
